candidate.title: P^3: Joint Program-and-Proof Planning for Verified Code Generation

verified_claims: Across Verina, AlgoVeri, and Lean4Commit0 with four frontier LLM backends, P^3 reports the highest solve rate in all 12 benchmark-model cells.
Compared with the stronger primary baseline, reported solve-rate gains are 4.6 to 11.2 percentage points.

The targeted implementation-only-planning ablation reports P^3 gains of 3.3 to 8.3 percentage points, directly supporting the marginal value of jointly planning program and proof rather than planning only the implementation.

On difficult-task subsets selected as the top 25% of tasks by mean cost across methods, the paper reports API-cost reduction of 3.0-39.6% and wall-clock reduction of 3.1-37.2%; these efficiency claims are subset-scoped and should not be generalized to all tasks.
Lean4Commit0 is repository-derived from 108 open-source libraries and contains 511 implementation placeholders plus 519 theorem placeholders with relational API specifications.
All methods use the same task instructions, API budget, time limit, maximum feedback-iteration budget, Docker image, and Lean version; each task-model-method cell is run once.
The paper states that complete prompts, harness, scripts, pinned environment, and run metadata are publicly available through a Figshare artifact.
important_limits: Each task-model-method configuration is run once, so the reported rates do not estimate within-task variance or multi-seed effect robustness.
The paper is very recent and no independent replication was verified in this comparator pass.
The strongest causal evidence isolates joint planning versus implementation-only planning, not every individual internal component of the P^3 workflow.

Efficiency gains are reported on a post-selected difficult subset (top 25% by mean cost across methods); the all-solved intersection is described as broadly comparable and can show planning overhead on easier cells.
Benchmark specification quality is filtered with reference behavior, mutation rejection, and an LLM review component; the authors themselves describe the specification gates as imperfect.
Transfer is explicitly limited to Lean 4, closed-source backends, Python-skewed repository APIs, and the tested benchmark/task distributions.

assessment.reason: Primary v1 directly verifies cross-model/cross-benchmark gains under fixed harness/budget and a targeted Plan-Seq versus P^3 ablation isolating joint program-and-proof planning. Public prompts/harness/scripts/pinned-environment/run-metadata materially strengthen reproducibility support. Keep A- rather than A because the study is a very recent preprint with single-run cells, no verified independent replication, imperfect specification gates, and subset-scoped efficiency results.
assessment.scope: Joint program-and-proof planning for Lean verified-code generation on the reported Verina, AlgoVeri, and Lean4Commit0 configurations and four frontier closed-source backends. Do not generalize to theorem proving broadly, open/smaller models, repeated-run reliability, or all efficiency regimes.
